title: Damp Stamp
tagline: Make the soil damp, not swamp.
concept: A turn-based shape-fitting puzzle about stamping measured sprays across thirsty soil without watering any patch twice.
core_loop: Choose a spray shape, rotate it, preview it over the soil, then pour; each satisfying 5–15 second placement darkens a clean patch and makes the remaining puzzle tighter.
mechanics: Controls: tap a spray card, Rotate, and a large soil cell, then tap Pour; keyboard players use 1–3, R, arrow keys, and Space, with an on-screen Undo button or U for the previous pour.; Win/lose: darken every pale tile exactly once before the visible can meter empties; previews crossing wet soil or the pot edge are blocked, and running out with dry tiles remaining loses the round.; Scoring: earn one leaf for clearing the pot, one for using no undo, and one for finishing with the displayed minimum number of pours.
feedback: A legal preview glows blue, poured soil darkens with a soft plop, and completed patches sprout tiny green shoots; an illegal preview turns red and the can gives a dry clunk, while a nearly empty can wobbles and remaining thirsty tiles pulse pale. On victory the whole plant perks up with a crisp chime; on failure the empty can rattles and Restart and Undo pulse immediately.
difficulty: The first minute uses small square beds, one obvious spray shape, and highlighted legal placements; later pots become larger and irregular, offer mixed rotatable shapes, include visible pre-damp no-go tiles, and tighten the pour budget without adding a timer or hidden rules.
